\begin{theorem}[A power bound for natural numbers]
\lean{Complexity.Meyer.pow_succ_ge}
\label{Complexity.Meyer.pow_succ_ge}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
For all natural numbers $n$ and $c$, $n^c+n\le (n+1)^{c+1}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Sufficient width bound]
\lean{Complexity.Meyer.width_ok}
\label{Complexity.Meyer.width_ok}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Meyer.pow_succ_ge, Complexity.Meyer.wd}
\difficulty{5}
For all natural numbers $c_0,c,n$, set $W=(c_0+3)(n+1)^{c+1}$. Then $n+2<2^W$ and
$c_0(2^n)^c\le 2^W-1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Membership characterized by the final configuration]
\lean{Complexity.Meyer.mem_iff_final}
\label{Complexity.Meyer.mem_iff_final}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Meyer.SS, Complexity.Meyer.wd, Complexity.Meyer.width_ok, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.OutReg.ofList, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.mono, Turing.FinTM.DecidesInTime, Turing.FinTM.computesInTime_iff, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom}
\difficulty{4}
Let $L$ be a language of Boolean words, let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over Boolean
symbols, and let $c_0,c$ be natural numbers. Suppose $M$ decides $L$ within the time
bound $n\mapsto c_0\,2^{n^c}$. Then for every Boolean word $x$, $x\in L$ if and only if,
after $2^{(c_0+3)(|x|+1)^{c+1}}-1$ steps from its initial configuration on $x$, the
machine is halted and its output register contains exactly the single bit $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Circuit description length bound]
\lean{Complexity.Meyer.desc_len_le}
\label{Complexity.Meyer.desc_len_le}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.encode, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.length_encode_le_of_isFaninTwo, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.size, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuitFamily, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuitFamily.HasFaninTwo, Complexity.Meyer.wd}
\difficulty{5}
Let $a,k,C_w,c_w,n_b$ be natural numbers, and let $F$ be a family of directed acyclic
Boolean circuits whose gates are well formed and have at most two inputs. Suppose every
circuit in the family has size at most $a(n+1)^k$ on inputs of length $n$. Define
$W(n)=C_w(n+1)^{c_w}$. Then the encoding length, plus one, of the circuit for input
length $n_b+4W(n)+4+n$ is at most
$\bigl(12a^2(n_b+4C_w+6)^{2k}+1\bigr)(n+1)^{2(c_w+1)k}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Length-consistency test on encoded inputs]
\lean{Complexity.Meyer.lenAll_inst}
\label{Complexity.Meyer.lenAll_inst}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Meyer.bjw, Complexity.Meyer.evalAtom, Complexity.Meyer.length_enumWord, Complexity.Meyer.va_vin, Complexity.Meyer.vin, Complexity.Meyer.vj_vin, Complexity.Meyer.vp_vin, Complexity.Meyer.vt_vin, Complexity.Meyer.vx_vin, Complexity.Meyer.wd, Complexity.enumWord, Turing.FinTM}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $C_w,c_w$ be natural
numbers, and let $x,U$ be finite binary strings. For natural numbers $t,a,j$ satisfying
$j\le |x|+1$ and $j<2^{C_w(|x|+1)^{c_w}}$, the length-consistency atom evaluates to true
on the encoded tuple formed from $x,U$, the width-$C_w(|x|+1)^{c_w}$ binary words for
$t$ and $a$, the string of $j$ ones, and a string of $C_w(|x|+1)^{c_w}-\ell$ zeros,
where $\ell$ is the binary length of $j$.
\end{theorem}
